Status icons, part of the play frame (reached from $2565 when $1112 is clear). Works out the sprite pointer of each of the eight icons along the bottom of the screen ($1188-$118F, drawn by the multiplexer): icons 1 to 7 come from the seven weapon levels at $0F00-$0F06, each through its own small table of frames ($0F07-$0F19), with the level XORed by a blink bit ($0F1C-$0F22) so that an icon being bought blinks between two frames; icon 0 is frame $8D plus the credit count ($107C). In the shop during play ($11AE and $1288), the shop sprites' colours ($91-$97) are set to grey ($0C) and the first n, n being the credits, to light blue ($0E): those are the icons the player can afford. Then runs the blink of the icon being bought ($0F23 blinks left, $0F24 which icon): when the blinks run out the purchase takes effect, icon 1's level counting 0-3 and back to 0, icon 2's up to 2, the others set to 1. Continues into the sprite-animation step at $0901.

Copies an animation frame number into each of seven sprite slots ($1190+x from the table at $0F2D, indexed by each slot's frame index at $0F25+x), then on alternate frames ($0F2F toggles) steps the per-slot counters $0F36/$0F2F/$0F45 that advance or reset those frame indexes; slots whose counters run out are reloaded from $0F3D and $0EFF. Latches a title key: $0FFB = $FF and $10B7 = 1, so the key acts once until everything is released, then leaves the interrupt.

If it beats none, $12FD is cleared.

Start-up and return to the title: sets $11A9 and the key latch $10B7, clears the sprite tables, $0FFB, the three $0FE8 flags and $0F78, resets the $1110 block, the bullets and $3F52, marks the game as not running ($0FFE = 0) and points the jump at $3B85 to $1768.

Start of a game, from the title: clears both players' scores ($11C0-$11C5, $11D0-$11D5, $9FB9-$9FBE) and $11D6, $9FB8, $9FC9; sets the current player to 1 ($11AB); gives lives: with two players ($12CA set) 3 each ($12CB and $1228), with one player 0 for player 2 and 3 for player 1; draws both players' lives (draw_lives) and both scores (s_3D31, once per player), then leaves the interrupt.

Between the title and play, by step Y (from $1C63): step 2, once $112A is clear, runs $385D, marks the game running ($0FFE), patches the code for play and sets $116D and $117F; otherwise, when $116D is clear, sets up the first stage (wave_setup_start), sets $107F, $12C8, $114A, $0FFF, starts the music (s_9E50 with A = 1), sets $1149 = $60, $1087 = 3 and clears $0FFE again.

Game-over sequence step, by $43C6: 0 goes to $9570; 1 waits for $112C and $112A to clear, then sets $0FFF and $43E3, returns to the title state (title_init) and moves to step 2; 2 resets the title state and clears $43C6 and $11AE.
Starts the game-over sequence: sets $112A, $112C and $43C6 to 1, clears $1087, and goes on at $2ABD.
$175E-$1767: two zero bytes, then LDA #$37 / STA $01 / JMP $FE66 (bank the ROMs back in and run the KERNAL's warm start), and a zero. No instruction reaches it.
Common end of every raster band handler: restores Y, X and A from the stack and returns from the interrupt.

The game's entry point, reached from the last unpacker. Sets the stack, masks interrupts, banks out BASIC and the KERNAL (keeping I/O, $01 = $35), stops CIA 1's timer A, points the raster chain at $1888 (pointer $1000/$1001), blanks the screen, raster interrupt at line $2E, black border and background, all sprites on and multicolour, screen at $4400 and characters at $4800 in VIC bank 1 ($DD00 = $96), 38 columns with scroll 7; clears the screen, sets up the title (title_init, title_state_reset), starts tune $0B, enables interrupts and enters the main loop.
The main loop: waits for raster line $E4, runs the sound for this frame (sfx_queue_service, $9D60), waits for the line to pass, and repeats. Everything else runs in the raster interrupts.
Three unused bytes: BRK, NOP, NOP.
Sets the processor port to $35 (RAM at $A000 and $E000, I/O at $D000) and returns with A = 0.

The hardware IRQ handler ($FFFE points here): saves A, X and Y, acknowledges the raster interrupt and jumps through the band pointer at $1000/$1001, which each band handler rewrites (high byte fixed at $18) to choose the next one. The handlers end at irq_exit. Each band handler is entered through a JMP stub in this page ($185E-$18EB), so one byte names it.
A padding NOP byte between the handler and the first band.

Band: next at line $5B, handler $1837; runs $2000.

Band: Y positions of sprites 5-8 from $113C plus $12C7, next band and line from $12C3/$12C2, and runs $9480 unless $1148 is set.

Writes $2E through the pointers at $4D, $53 and $55 (offset 1), then leaves the interrupt.
With two players ($12CA) and $1080 clear, counts $107F up and goes to $3918; otherwise to $3A7F.
Ten NOPs after jmp_19c2, unused.
Band at the top of the play frame ($18A0): blanks the screen ($D011 = $40), next band $1888 at line $2D, runs the per-frame game step $9100 and then $9A30.

Title band ($18A6), line $1F -> next $18A9: screen blanked, all sprite pointers to frame $9B, X and Y of the eight sprites from $43C8 and $0FE0, the stars (s_1DB9); while a key has just been pressed ($0FFB) shows the three option sprites (players $43C0, controls $43C2, music $43C4 by $12CA, $0FFC, $0FFD) in sprites 5-7. Then by $0FFE: 0 goes to $9710, 1 starts the game (game_start_scores), 2+ goes on with interlude_game_start.
Title band ($18A9), line $2E -> next $180E: sets the sprite pointers at $47F8-$47FC to 8-12.
Eight NOPs after irq_title_1c80, unused.
Places the title logo's top sprites: pointers $3A/$3B in sprites 0-1 at Y $7B, X $CF and $E7, sprites 3 and 4 at Y $7B with pointers $38/$39, then next band $18AC at line $8B.
When $116D is clear: stores Y in $112E, sets the speed jumps and goes on at $3A15; otherwise $3FE3.
If $129B is set, sets $129A to 1.
Erases the stars: writes the blank character $2E at the eighteen screen positions listed at $100A-$101B, in each of the four quarters of the screen ($43F8, $44F8, $45F8, $46F8 + offset).

Middle star layer, one pixel a frame: rotates the single set bit of glyph $30's fourth row ($4983) left; when it falls out, puts it back at the right of the glyph ($FE) and moves the six stars of this layer one column left (their screen offsets $1010-$1015).
Fast star layer, two pixels a frame: rotates the bit in glyph $31's seventh row ($498E) left twice; when it falls out, resets it and moves the six stars of this layer ($1016-$101B) one column left.
Slow star layer: rotates the bit in glyph $2F's first row ($4978) left; when it falls out, resets it and moves the six stars of this layer ($100A-$100F) one column left. Called every second frame.
Draws the three star layers at their new screen offsets in all four quarters of the screen: character $B1 for the offsets at $1016-$101B, $30 for $1010-$1015 and $6F for $100A-$100F.

The scrolling starfield, once a frame on the title and in play: erases the stars, steps the colour-cycle (s_257C), moves the middle and fast layers, the slow layer every second frame ($101C toggles), and draws them again. Each star is one character whose glyph holds a single pixel; rolling that pixel through the glyph moves every star of the layer smoothly, and the character moves a column when the pixel wraps.
Every fourth frame ($101D counts to 4) steps a six-entry colour cycle ($101E) and copies the current entry of four colour tables ($101F, $1025, $102B, $1031) into $12D6-$12D9.

When a player's game ends: sets the name-entry state ($1149 = $40, $114A, $1080, $107E, $107F, $1148 = 1), the four name-entry sprite colours $11A0-$11A3 (14, 15, 16, 10), writes the player's digit into the text 'PLAYER n' ($FBC7 = $1E + player, the digit 1 or 2 in the game's alphabet), runs $9980 and tries the score against the high-score table (hiscore_insert), then $3FE3.

High-score name entry, once a frame while $1148 is set, by its value: 1 decides whether the score made the table ($12FD): if not, goes on to the next player ($3E0F, with two players and the other still alive) or game over ($9EF8); if so, sets up the entry sprites ($91E0, $1E7E). 2 waits at $27C0. 3 and up reads the controls: fire moves to the next of the eight letters ($12FF) and after the eighth copies the name into the player's name store and ends the entry; left/right and up/down (with key repeat delays) step the current letter forwards or back through the 29 symbols (A-Z, '.', '(c)', space).
Places the eight name-entry sprites: X from $0FC0, Y $80, high bits clear, pointers $28-$2F, then moves the entry to its next state.

End of name entry: clears the cursor sprite bytes, copies the eight letters from the table slot ($F7F0 + $12FE) into the player's name store ($F0D0 or $F0D8), then goes on to the other player ($9EF0) in a two-player game with lives left, or to game over.
Y = $12FE + $12FF: the offset of the letter being entered in the high-score table at $F7F0.
Key repeat for the name entry: left or right held counts $110B to 6 and then sets $1171 (previous letter) or $1170 (next letter); up or down counts $114F to 3, setting $1171 or $1170.
hiscore_repeat: right held.
hiscore_repeat: up held.
hiscore_repeat: down held.
Two RTS bytes and thirty zero bytes, unused.
Sets the name-entry cursor: $116E = (letter position AND 6), $11A7 = that / 2 + 8 (the cursor sprite's frame), and $116D.
When not in the game-over sequence ($43C6 clear) goes to $9CC8, else to $3FE3.

Band for the hazard row at the top of the play area (from $182A): puts sprites 1-7 on line $47 and sets their frames from $BF-$C5, then $3550. The top and bottom rows each reuse the seven sprites the multiplexer frees there.
Band for the hazard row at the bottom of the play area (from $1851): sprites 1-7 on line $E0, frames from $CD-$D3, then $221E (the score adder and $9968).

Every eighth frame ($1037 counts 0-7), with all RAM banked in ($01 = $34) to read the tables under the I/O area: on the counter's zero goes to $952F; otherwise returns. Entered as hazard_rows_spawn at $2096 with A = $103A to start new hazards: for the top row ($1038, $1090) and the bottom row ($1039, $1098), takes the next entry of the section's spawn list at $D500 (a zero ends it), finds a free slot of seven, sets its bit in $1078/$1079, marks it busy, gives it the X start $4F and looks up its animation start in the tables at $D000/$D100 (s_97E0, s_9820 / s_9860, s_9890). $103C counts the rows down. Banks the I/O back in ($01 = $35) and leaves the interrupt.

Operand high byte of the spawn-list read in hazard_rows_spawn (LDA $D500,Y): the page of the stage's spawn list, patched by hazard_rows_config. Other routines compare it with $D5 to see whether the stage has hazards.
Operand high byte of the second spawn-list read (the next entry), patched with $20C7.
hazard_rows_spawn, bottom row: a free slot found; starts its hazard.
Operand high byte of the bottom row's spawn-list read, patched with $20C7.
Operand high byte of the bottom row's next-entry read, patched with $20C7.

Steps the interlude's colours: for $0FAD-$0FAE, $0FC8-$0FCB and the first animation frame, replaces each by its successor in the chain at $1119 (a table of next colours); counts in $1118 how many reached zero, and when all seven have, clears $0FCD (the fade is finished).

Interlude, by the state of title page $0FA9 ($0FE8 + page): 0 nothing; 1 puts that page's picture into the five big sprites (copy_sprite_rows_a/b/c); 2 advances the state, patches $3B91 to $40, resets the cursor (s_2210) and loads four colours $11A0-$11A3 from $1040 + 4 x page; 3 (when $116D is clear) advances, patches $3B91 to $4A and loads the colours from $104C; afterwards waits for $116D. All paths go on to $955B.
When X = 7 sets $12C0 to 3.
Clears $116E and $11A7 and sets $116D.
After the bottom row: adds the pending score into the score (s_232D) and goes on at $9968.

Takes the next of four colour sets for the interlude ($0FCF counts 0-3, clearing $0FCE when it wraps): $0FAD, $0FAE, $0FC8-$0FCB and the first animation frame from the tables at $1154, $1158, $115C, $1160, $1164 and $1168.

Buying in the shop: the ship has touched the shop's sprite X, whose price is X credits. If the shop is not up ($1288 clear), a purchase was already made in this shop ($12F7), or the credits ($107C) do not cover the price, the touch counts as a hit ($1087 = Y = 1): an unaffordable (grey) icon kills, and only one icon can be bought per shop. Otherwise keeps the change in $12FB, starts the icon's blink ($0F24 = X - 1, $0F23 = 14 blinks), sets $12F7, $12F9 and the icon's flag at $1221 + X, and goes on at $9EC4 (the sound).
shop_try_buy, the purchase itself: checks the price against the credits and starts the icon's blink.

While a purchase is being paid ($12F9): one credit a frame comes off $107C (unless $11AA); when they are all gone, clears $12F9 and adds the change ($12FB) to the hundreds digit of the score: every credit left over after the price is worth 100 points. Then $22BD.
Sets $0F1A to $89 + $12C0 (a frame number) and continues at $22F9.

Draws the current player's lives digit into the panel: the digit $12CB picks a 20-byte glyph from the table at $FEA4 (ten rows of two bytes), which is copied into every other two bytes of the sprite at $6600 + ($4F or $8F for player 1 or 2), thirty bytes in all.

Sets the opcode toggle at $34B7 from $12D5 and, unless the ship is mid-move ($1100, $1101), loads the ship's speed $1104/$1105 from the pair at $0FF1 + 2 x speed level ($0F00): speeds 1/1, 2/2, 4/4 and 8/8. Then on to the icons ($2560).
A = $F900 + Y, shifted right twice, into $D4; then $38C3.
Adds the pending score ($11D1-$11D5) into the score digits ($11C1-$11C5), digit by digit from the last, carrying tens into the digit before ($11D0 + x), and clears the pending digits; then $9CD6.

Sets hardware sprite 0, the player's ship: X, Y and frame from the first entries of the zero-page tables ($38, $40, $30), colour $90, and copies its X high bit ($28) into bit 0 of both high-bit masks $1078 and $1079.

Multiplexer step for the stage where $1084 is set (from irq_band_top): ship in sprite 0, multicolours from $10E0/$10E1, sprites 1-7 on line $32 with frames from $B8-$BE and X from $D9-$DF, X high bits from $1078, colour $10E2; then moves each active top-row hazard ($1090 + x) three pixels left, and when one passes X 0 either clears it (high bit already clear) or drops its high bit. Leaves the interrupt.
Operand of the SBC #$03 that moves the top hazard row left: the rows' speed, set to 0 while paused and 3 again after.
Eight NOPs after mux_upper_row_32, unused.

The same for the second row: line $103D, frames $C6-$CC, X $E1-$E7, high bits $1079, colour $10E2; moves the bottom-row hazards ($1098 + x) three pixels left the same way. Then, by $1084: 0 leaves the interrupt, 2 goes to $9B70, other values to $9968.
Operand of the bottom row's SBC #$03: its speed, zeroed while paused.

Sequence step before the name entry, by $1081: 0 does nothing; 1 sets $116D, advances $1081, sets the entry sprites' colours ($11A1/$11A3 = $18, $11A0 = 7 + $12FE / 8, $11A2 one more), points the jump at $3BB3 to $F7B0 and latches the keys; 2, once $116D clears, ends the step ($1081 = 0) and sets $112E. Every path goes on to swap_graphics_step.
When $1112 is set, blanks the icon row (all eight icon frames $8D, colours $0E) and goes on at $2BD2; otherwise updates the icons (icons_update).

Erases every object drawn with characters before they are drawn again: writes the blank character $2E through the pointers $1A-$26 (seven), $49/$4B/$4D, $51/$53/$55, $A0/$A2/$A4, the two cells of each of the six one-row shots ($E8-$F2) and the four cells of the two 2x2 objects ($F4, $F6, offsets 0, 1, 40, 41); then $3F9B.

Draws enemy shot 0 at the screen cell its pointer $E8 holds: takes the glyphs of the two background characters under it (their codes AND $3F, times 8, in the set at $4800), ANDs them with the shot's mask pair at $FF70/$FF78 shifted by its sub-cell position ($10A0), writes the result into the shot's own two glyphs ($D0/$D1 at $4880-$488F) and puts those characters on the screen. The shot so appears over the stars and anything else beneath, at any pixel position.
As draw_enemy_shot_0 for shot 1: pointer $EA, position $10A1, glyphs $D2/$D3 at $4890.
As draw_enemy_shot_0 for shot 2: pointer $EC, position $10A2, glyphs $C8/$C9 at $4840.
As draw_enemy_shot_0 for shot 3: pointer $EE, position $10A3, glyphs $CA/$CB at $4850.
As draw_enemy_shot_0 for shot 4: pointer $F0, position $10A4, glyphs $CC/$CD at $4860.
As draw_enemy_shot_0 for shot 5: pointer $F2, position $10A5, glyphs $CE/$CF at $4870.
Waits in the name entry while $1081 is set; then hands $112E to $1EAA.

Moves and draws each active character object: the six one-row shots ($10AA-$10AF set: s_3021-s_31CA) and the two 2x2 objects ($10A8, $10A9: s_321F, s_32CA). Then draws three fixed characters ($32, $33, $34 through $A0, $A2, $A4) and three two-cell pairs ($FE/$FF, $FC/$FD, $FA/$FB through $49, $4B, $4D), and leaves the interrupt.

Draws enemy bomb 0 (2x2 characters) at pointer $F4: builds glyphs $00-$03 ($4800-$481F) from the four cells beneath it, the rows above its pixel row $10A6 copied unchanged and the ball cut in from there with the mask table at $FF70 (the read's operands patched with $10B0, the position across the cell), so the bomb can sit at any pixel row and column; then puts the four characters ($C0-$C3) on the screen.
Operand low byte of the mask read for enemy bomb 0's first column ($FF70 + 8 x position), patched from $10B0.
Operand low byte of the mask read for bomb 0's second column.
Operand low byte of the mask read for bomb 0's third column.
Operand low byte of the mask read for bomb 0's fourth column.
As draw_enemy_bomb_0 for bomb 1: pointer $F6, pixel row $10A7, position $10B1 patched into the mask reads at $299C/$29A4/$29B9/$29C1, glyphs $04-$07 at $4820, characters $C4-$C7.
Operand low byte of the mask read for enemy bomb 1's first column, patched from $10B1.
Operand low byte of bomb 1's second mask column.
Operand low byte of bomb 1's third mask column.
Operand low byte of bomb 1's fourth mask column.

Sets the eight sprites for the score panel at the top: frames $95, $96, $99, $AB, $97, $98, $9A, $A9, all on line $16 at fixed X positions ($1F, $37, $55, $67, $EF, $07+256, $25+256, $37+256), colour 14; then $9AE5.
Immediate of LDY #$AB in irq_panel_sprites: player 1's panel ship frame, rewritten by panel_ship_spin (and set to $A9 by play_patches_on).
Immediate of LDY #$A9: player 2's panel ship frame, rewritten by panel_ship_spin.

Multiplexer for the main play area: ship in sprite 0, then sprites 1-7 from the zero-page tables (frame $30+x, X $38+x, Y $40+x, colour $90+x), X high bits $107A, multicolours $1082/$1083; then the colour cycle and $363B.
Rebuilds the X high-bit mask $107A from the eight per-sprite flags $28-$2F (bit x from $1088 + x) and leaves the interrupt.

Converts a sprite position into a screen address: Y ($05, rounded down to a character row) gives row x 40 + $4300 + 13, X ($04) / 8 the column, plus 32 more when the high bit ($06) is set; result in $02/$03. Used to look at the characters under a sprite.

How the player's weapons hit: every weapon is drawn with characters (glyphs $32-$3F), so for each of the seven enemy sprites that is alive ($11E0), not exploding ($12A8) and not final ($1208), the four screen cells under it are read (offsets 0, 1, 40, 41 from sprite_to_screen_ptr). A glyph of $32 or above is a weapon: the enemy is hit ($1070 + x = 1) and the glyph's low nibble picks a handler from $0F50 that ends the weapon that hit it (laser bolts 1-3, the two beams, the three extra shots; the orbiter, nibble 5, is not used up but marks $129D). Then $9C0C.

Handlers for an enemy touching a weapon character, by its glyph's low nibble: $2B7C laser bolt 1 ($FE/$FF: column $24 ends it), $2B84 bolt 2 ($FC/$FD), $2B8C bolt 3 ($FA/$FB), $2B94 the upper beam ($F8/$F9), $2B9C the lower beam ($F6/$F7), $2BA4 the extra weapon's upward shot ($32), $2BAC its backward shot ($33), $2BB4 its downward shot ($34); each then goes to $2CC4.

How enemy fire hits the ship: clears $1087, then sets it if the cell 41 bytes on from the ship's cell pointer $71 (under the middle of the ship) holds a glyph below $2E, which are exactly the enemy fire's glyphs (the shots and bombs at $00-$13, the bullet $ED = glyph $2D). Then the controls.
Immediate of the CMP #$2E in ship_hit_by_fire (glyphs below it are enemy fire); the unreached cheat at $BA00 would set it to 0, so nothing could hit the ship.

When the ship is in the shop and its sprite collides with an icon sprite ($48 bit 0 and the icon's bit): checks the distance from the ship to each icon (Y within 20, X within 24, either side of the high bit) and tries to buy it (shop_try_buy). Then $9C00.
Immediate of the AND #$01 in ship_touch_icons (the ship's collision bit); the unreached cheat at $BA00 toggles it.

Unless $12CC is set: copies the slow-down's state ($0F2F if icon 6 is owned, else 0) to $107B and runs the attack wave ($8010); then the enemy update ($3C89), and sets $1087 when the ship's sprite collides with anything ($1117 or $112B bit 0). Goes on at $3880.
Two NOP bytes ahead of orbiter_draw; nothing runs them.

The orbiter (icon 5, $0F04; $10D8 set by orbiter_step): draws character $B5 at the screen cell two rows above and two columns left of the ship's cell ($71 - $52) moved on by the offsets $10B8 (columns) and $10C0 (rows, 40 each) from the circle table; a position off the play area (rows above $4400 or past $47E8, or the ship near the top) falls back to the ship's own cell. The pointer $51 is erased next frame by erase_char_objects. Then the enemy bullets.
Runs the hazard-row frame step (s_9480) unless $107F and $12C8 are both other than 1.
Stores A in $129D and goes back into enemies_hit_by_weapons, which marks the enemy hit.
A padding NOP.

Enemy bullet 0 (one of seven drawn as the character $ED): while active ($10D9) moves its screen pointer $1A by its column step $10B9 (signed, whole cells) within columns 0-40 ($10C9) and by its row step $10C1 (40 a row) within rows 0-23 ($10D1), then draws $ED there. Leaving the screen ends it ($10D9 cleared) through bullet_chain_1. Falls through to the next bullet's mover.
As bullet_move_0 for enemy bullet 1: flag $10DA, steps $10BA/$10C2, column $10CA, row $10D2, pointer $1C.
As bullet_move_0 for enemy bullet 2: flag $10DB, steps $10BB/$10C3, column $10CB, row $10D3, pointer $1E.
As bullet_move_0 for enemy bullet 3: flag $10DC, steps $10BC/$10C4, column $10CC, row $10D4, pointer $20.
As bullet_move_0 for enemy bullet 4: flag $10DD, steps $10BD/$10C5, column $10CD, row $10D5, pointer $22.
As bullet_move_0 for enemy bullet 5: flag $10DE, steps $10BE/$10C6, column $10CE, row $10D6, pointer $24.
As bullet_move_0 for enemy bullet 6: flag $10DF, steps $10BF/$10C7, column $10CF, row $10D7, pointer $26.
Also read as data: enemy_ai_step takes its pseudo-random numbers from the 256 bytes starting here, which are this code (bullet_move_6 and the enemy-shot movers).

Moves enemy shot 0 along its row: the signed speed $10E6 is added to its sub-cell position $10A0 (128 steps a cell); on a carry the shot moves one cell right (or left, for a negative speed), stepping its column $10EE and its screen pointer $E8. At column 40 (moving right) or 0 (moving left) the shot ends: $10AA is cleared and $3FAA runs. Then the shot is drawn (draw_enemy_shot_0).
As move_enemy_shot_0 for shot 1: speed $10E7, column $10EF, position $10A1, pointer $EA, active flag $10AB, drawn by draw_enemy_shot_1.
As move_enemy_shot_0 for shot 2: speed $10E8, column $10F0, position $10A2, pointer $EC, active flag $10AC, drawn by draw_enemy_shot_2.
As move_enemy_shot_0 for shot 3: speed $10E9, column $10F1, position $10A3, pointer $EE, active flag $10AD, drawn by draw_enemy_shot_3.
As move_enemy_shot_0 for shot 4: speed $10EA, column $10F2, position $10A4, pointer $F0, active flag $10AE, drawn by draw_enemy_shot_4.
As move_enemy_shot_0 for shot 5: speed $10EB, column $10F3, position $10A5, pointer $F2, active flag $10AF, drawn by draw_enemy_shot_5.

Moves enemy bomb 0 (one of two 2x2-character shots that travel at an angle): horizontally as the shots do (speed $10EC, position $10B0, column $10F4, pointer $F4), then vertically (speed $10F6 added to the pixel row $10A6, eight rows a cell, row $10F8 from 0 to 22, the pointer moving by 40); leaving the screen at either edge ends it ($10A8 cleared, then $3FB9). Drawn by draw_enemy_bomb_0.
As move_enemy_bomb_0 for bomb 1: speeds $10ED/$10F7, positions $10B1/$10A7, column $10F5, row $10F9, pointer $F6, flag $10A9, drawn by draw_enemy_bomb_1.

Reads both joysticks into the five control flags (1 when pressed): $10FA fire, $10FB up, $10FC down, $10FD left, $10FE right. The CIA 1 interrupt is masked while it reads; port 1 ($DC01) and port 2 ($DC00) are read in turn through $DBFF + Y and ORed, so either port works. Game start patches the base of the read ($3389/$338A).
Operand low byte of the joystick read in read_joysticks (LDA $DBFF,Y): $FF for the real ports $DC00/$DC01, $90 for the demo's recorded input at $0F91.
Operand high byte of the joystick read: $DB for the ports, $0F for the demo.
Converts a sprite position to a screen column and row: column = X ($04) / 8 - 3, plus 32 when the high bit ($06) is set, into $02; row = Y ($05) / 8 - 6 into $03.

Moves the player's ship from the control flags. Up and down move it in steps of eight pixels: a press starts a step ($1100 or $1101 = 8) unless the ship is at the top (Y $36) or bottom (Y $DE), and each frame the step advances by the speed, alternating between the two speed bytes $1104/$1105 ($1106 toggles) until the eight pixels are done. Left and right move it by the speed every frame (alternating $1104/$1105 by $1107), between X $24 and X $130 (high bit $28). Then $3F10.

Fire: counts the fire delay $1109 down; a new press (the latch $1108 is cleared when fire is released) fires when the delay is over and shots are left ($110A, plus the fire-rate level $0F01 must reach 3): takes a free laser slot of three ($110B-$110D), starts it at the ship's column ($8D into $110E + slot) one row down and one column right of the ship's screen cell ($71 + $29, into the pointers $49/$4B/$4D), sets the delay to 8 and queues the laser sound ($9E68). Then the extra weapon ($3502).
An opcode byte in ship_fire, written from $12D5 by ship_speed_set; as the game leaves $12D5 alone it stays as loaded.

The bought extra weapon (icon 3, $0F02): when it is owned and no burst is in flight ($1113), fires three shots at once from around the ship: one forward-low that travels left from one cell right of the ship ($A2, counted by $1115 from the ship's column), one upwards ($A0, $1114 from the ship's row) and one downwards ($A4, $1116 = row + 3); $1113 counts the three still flying. Queues its sound ($9E70).
After the top hazard row: with $1084 = 2 runs the hazard frame step (wave_tail_9480), then leaves the interrupt.
Stores Y in $1117 and $48 (clears the recorded sprite collisions).

Moves each of the three laser bolts in flight ($110B + slot): one cell right a frame, counting its column $110E + slot to $24, where it ends (slot freed, a shot returned to $110A, its cell blanked and its pointer parked at $47F0). Then the extra weapon's shots ($35AD).
One laser bolt, slot Y: moves its screen pointer one cell right and its column on, or ends it at column $24.
laser_step: the bolt reached column $24: frees the slot, returns the shot, blanks its cell and parks its pointer.

Moves the extra weapon's three shots while the burst lasts ($1113): the left-going one ($A2) one cell left a frame until its count $1115 runs out, the upward one ($A0) one row up until $1114 runs out, the downward one ($A4) one row down until $1116 reaches $18 (row 24); each that finishes is parked ($80 in its count, pointer $47F0) and decrements $1113. Then $3EBD.
Copies the play area's colours to the VIC: background $12D6, multicolours $12D7 and $12D8, extended colour $12D9; then $3CBC.

Every fourth frame ($1129): runs whichever colour fades are under way: the sprite fade ($112A, s_3771), the colour-set step ($112E, s_37A5), the row-sprite fade ($112C, s_37CE), the interlude fade ($0FCD) and the interlude colour set ($0FCE). Then, during play ($11AE): in the shop ($1288) keeps the timer $12FA loaded; after it, counts $12FA down and turns any credits left into points (they are paid off one a frame by shop_spend_step).
Puts the eight icon sprites along the bottom: frames from $1188-$118F, Y $B4 (patched at $36EE), X positions $1F, $47, $6F, $97, $BF, $E7, $0F and $37 (the last two past 256).
Immediate of the LDY #$B4 in icons_sprites_set: the icons' Y position ($B4 in play, rewritten for the title).
Sets the eight icon sprites' colours from $1190-$1197 and the multicolours from $1082 and $0FCB (the operands at $3765 and $376B are patched for play and the title).
Operand low byte of the LDY $1082 in icons_colours_set, patched to $5E or $82 for the title or play.
Operand low byte of the LDY $0FCB in icons_colours_set, patched to $5F or $CB.
Operand high byte of that LDY, patched to $10 or $0F.
Fades the sprite colours: each of $1082/$1083 and the colours $90-$97 steps to its successor in the colour chain at $1119; when all ten are zero (black) clears $112A.
Takes the next of four colour sets ($114D counts, clearing $112E after the fourth): multicolours $1082/$1083 from $1150/$1180 and all eight sprite colours from $1184.
Fades the three row colours $10E0-$10E2 through the colour chain; when all are black clears $112C.

Sets up the banner for the next stage: writes the stage number ($107D + 1) as two digits in the game's alphabet into the text at $EB86/$EB87, and takes the stage's two colours from the table at $F880 (two bytes a stage: low nibble + 4 into $11A1, high nibble into $11A0, the second byte to $9993).
Clears the attack-wave state: $12CC, the seven enemies' alive, live, exploding and movement entries ($11E0, $1248, $12A8, $11E8, $11F0), $128D and $128E, sets $128B, and goes to $9B7C with A = 7.
Sets the banner's sprite colours ($11A0-$11A3 = 11, 12, 13, 10) and writes the current player's digit into 'PLAYER n' ($FBC7), then $9980.

The shield (icon 7, $0F06): for 16 frames after a hit ($12FC) the ship cannot be hit again ($1087 cleared). While the shield is owned, a hit ($1087) is absorbed instead of killing the ship: it costs one of the shield's charges ($12C0, three when bought) and starts the 16 frames; the last charge removes the shield. Then $39C9.

Second half of a stage's hazard setup: from the stage table at $F900 (four bytes a stage), the bottom row's count ($1039, high nibble of byte 2) and the high byte of the spawn list ($20C7 and three more operands patched to it).
Loads the seven enemy sprites' frame, X (plus $12C4) and Y from the tables at $1130, $1138 and $1140, clears their X high bits and colours, and clears $107A, $1082, $1083.
Clears the X positions and X high bits of sprites 1-7 and the mask $107A; returns A = 0.

Starts a stage's hazard rows: if $12C1 is zero just sets $103C; otherwise sets $1084 to it, both rows' counts to 1, and from the stage table at $F900 (byte 1: the two multicolours $10E0/$10E1, byte 2: the colour $10E2) and hazard_rows_config; clears both rows.
hazards_stage_setup with rows: sets the row count and both rows on, takes the rows' colours and spawn page from the stage table and clears the rows.
Clears the fourteen hazard slots (X $D8-$DF and $E0-$E7, busy flags $1090/$1098) and both high-bit masks $1078/$1079.
Clears the ship's weapons when it dies: $110F-$1111 to $24, the extra weapon's counts to 0 unless parked, $1116 to $18, blanks the lasers' cells, then $3F35.
Clears $0F70-$0F73, then $9D35.

Ship-death sequence, by $107E: 0 carries on to $3A06; 1 starts it ($112A set, weapons cleared, $107E = 2) and sets $112C unless $1080 or $1084 is clear; 2 waits for both fades ($112A, $112C) to finish and then resets $107E.
death_sequence_step, state 2: waits for both fades to finish, then clears the state.

Stage start sequence, by $107F: 0 goes on to the death sequence ($3AE8); 1 sets up the bands for the stage ($1CE0 -> $3A15); 2, once $112E is clear, counts the banner timer $1149/$114A down and, at zero, ends the banner ($43D6, fade $112A) and moves on; 3+ waits for the fade, then sets up the stage's waves (s_9BD0) and the band restart for its number of hazard rows ($12C1: none, one or two).

Sets the raster chain for a stage by its hazard rows ($12C1, or $1084): with none, the chain restarts at line $7E with $18C8 and the bottom at $F3/$18D0; with one, the top row at $47 ($1867) and the other at $E0 with the bottom at $DD/$1874; with two, $45/$182A, $CB and $C5/$1844. Loads the sprite template (s_38DD), sets $12CC and clears $11A9. Then $19C2.
Moves the stage start on ($107F) and, until $1084 reaches $12C1, starts the next hazard row (hazards_stage_setup).

After a death, by $12C8: 0 goes to the high-score step; 1 places a fresh ship (frame from the stage, ship_reset_position), and re-arms the hazard rows if the stage has any; 2+ waits for $112E, then clears $12C8 and $1080 and $0F70-$0F73.
Stage clear, by $129B: 0 goes to the orbiter ($3E5E); 1 clears the collisions and goes to $91EF; 2+ clears $129B and $1087 and runs $9BC8.

Starts the next stage: its number of hazard rows ($12C1) from the low two bits of the stage table at $F900 + 4 x $107D, the stage-start, death and banner states to 1, the banner timer to $0180, $129B on, and the stage banner (stage_banner_setup).

Draws the banner text into the eight banner sprites, one character per call while $116D is set (else it leaves the interrupt through the patched jump at $3B85): the line $11A0 + (progress / 4) holds an index into the message table ($F7B0, patched at $3BB3), eight letters a line; each letter's 20-byte glyph from the font at $FC60 is copied into the sprite at $4A00/$4A21 (two letters a sprite, the second shifted four pixels across). $116E counts the letters 0-7 and $11A7 the progress 0-15; at 16 the banner is complete and $116D clears.
Operand low byte of the JMP at $3B85 in banner_draw_step: where to go when no banner is drawing: $1768 (irq_exit) on the title, $3C7A in play.
Operand high byte of that JMP ($17 or $3C).
Immediate of the LDA #$4A in banner_draw_step: the high byte of the banner sprites' address ($4A00, or $40 for the interlude's pictures).
Operand low byte of the message-table read (LDA $F7B0,Y) in banner_draw_step: which message table the banner draws from.
Operand high byte of the message-table read: $F7B0 title texts, $FB70 messages, $EB80 stage words.
Target of the patched jump at $3B85 during play: counts $11A8 down into $116D (keeps the banner drawing a while longer), then the orbiter ($2C51).
Animates two of the eight sprites a frame ($11AA steps by two): each sprite's frame comes from its animation list at $1300 + position ($11B0 + x), restarting at $11B8 + x when the list gives $FF.

The current player's small ship in the score panel spins during play: $11AC starts it ($11AE set, position $11C0 = 0), and every four frames ($11AF) the next frame from the list at $1312 ($A9-$AF) is written into the panel code's immediate at $2A06 (player 1) or $2A19 (player 2). A death sets $11AD, which stops it when the list comes round to its start. Then $9ADA.
$3D13-$3D30: LDA #$35 / STA $01 / JMP $22F6, then a colour-fade loop over $10E0-$10E7 like row_fade_step. No instruction reaches it.

Draws the current player's six score digits into the panel sprites: each digit's eight-byte glyph from $FB20 + digit x 8 goes into the sprite bytes at $6564 + offset, three bytes apart (one sprite column), the offset for each digit from $11C5 (player 1) or $11CA (player 2).

Prepares the banner: clears the letter and progress counters, sets $11A8, and for each of the four lines counts the trailing spaces ($1C) of its eight letters at $FB70 + line x 8, six pixels each, into $12C4-$12C7, the indent that centres the line.
Operand low byte of the message-table read in banner_centre, patched together with $3BB4.
Operand high byte of banner_centre's message-table read.

The ship being hit, by $1087: 0 goes to the stage-clear step; 1 starts the explosion ($11AD, animation from position 2), sets $11D0 = $40 frames, takes a life ($12CB), queues the sound, picks a new attack pattern (s_3F7D) and resets $12C9; 2 waits out the $40 frames, then with no lives left goes to game over and the name entry, with two players and the other alive changes turn (swap_players), otherwise restarts the stage for the same player; the stage restart sets the banner and the start states.
Hands the game to the other player: their hazard rows ($1229 into $12C1 and $1084), swap_players, $1080 cleared, then the restart at $3E37.
ship_death_step, same player continues: sets $1080 and the row count again, then the banner and stage-start states.

The orbiter (icon 5, $0F04): while owned and not held by $12CD, sets $10D8 and takes the next of sixteen offsets round the ship from the circle table at $FB00 (columns into $10B8, rows into $10C0, $12CE stepping by two); then the weapon-hit check.

Weapon 4 (icon 4, $0F03): when owned and neither of its beams is in flight ($12D0, $12D1), fires two: one at the ship's cell ($53) and one two rows below ($55), both from the ship's column ($12D2, $12D3); queues the sound ($9E78).
Moves weapon 4's two beams ($12D0, $12D1 active) and then the character objects (char_objects_step).
One beam of weapon 4: one cell right a frame until column $25, drawing characters $F8/$F9 (upper beam, $53) or $F6/$F7 (lower, $55); at the end it is blanked and freed.
Works out the ship's character cell from its sprite position (column into $8D, row into $8E) and the screen address of that cell ($71/$72), then fire (ship_fire).
End of ship_death_weapons: blanks weapon 4's beams, clears its flags, all sixteen character-object flags ($10A8-$10AF, $10D8-$10DF) and sets $12D4.
Points every character-object pointer at $4400 (the screen's first cell): the seven bullets ($1A-$26), the eight shots and big objects ($E8-$F6), and $51, $53, $55.

The attack wave's spawner, once a frame (from wave_step, and on the title's demo page): not on a slow-down frame ($107B). A pending wave type ($128E) dispatches through the table at $9F20 (type 1: $908F). Otherwise, while enemies of the current group are still to come ($128D), spawns the next into a free slot ($80C9); when the group is done and the delay $114B and the group's rule allow ($1298: all seven accounted for), starts the next group: takes the next entry of the stage's wave list ($B800 or $B900 + $129A), points $12F2/$12F3 and $08/$09 at its record ($AB00 + entry x 8) and its size ($1299). If no enemy of the finished group escaped ($128B clear), a group that carried a credit (bit 7 of its record's byte 3, $1289) adds one to the credits $107C; one marked with bit 6 ($128A) takes one away ($9ED4). Then the enemy movers ($9024).

Jump to the enemy movers ($9024).

Spawns the next enemy of the wave group into slot X: clears its state ($1210, $12B0, $11F8, $1200, $1208, $12E0 and the group flags $1288-$128B, $1298), reads the group's record through $12DE/$12DF (the entry at $B991 + $129A gives $FF at the end of the stage, which sets $129B unless $1087). Moves the seven enemies, one unrolled copy of the same code per slot ($82CC slot 1, $84B4 slot 2, $869C slot 3, $8884 slot 4, $8A6C slot 5, $8C54 slot 6, $8E3C slot 7). First counts down each slot's spawn delay ($1248 + x) and makes the enemy alive ($11E0, $1270) when it ends; on a slow-down frame ($107B) the paths are not stepped.

Slot 1's mover (the other six slots repeat it at $84B4, $869C, $8884, $8A6C, $8C54, $8E3C with their own variables). For a live enemy ($11E1): when its explosion ($12A9) has ended (frame $9B) frees the slot and counts it in $128C; when hit ($1071) takes a hit point ($1241, never from $FF): at zero it either changes into its next form, when bit 7 of its segment's byte 3 says so ($1219: new animation and hit points from the form list at $12FE + n, $FF there making it final, $1209), or explodes: animation position 2 (the explosion frames), its points added (s_9074, by $1281), marked exploding ($12A9). When an icon is touched in the shop ($1221), or it leaves the play area (Y outside $38-$E0, or past X $158), it is removed ($841D). Otherwise it follows its path: the path list ($1251/$1259) names segments (four bytes each at $A880 + 4n: a velocity list from $A080, the speed/fire byte $12E9, an animation offset added to $12A1, the frames per step with bit 7 = change form when killed), and the velocity list gives a (dx, dy) pair every $1279 frames, mirrored by $1211/$1291, into $11E9/$11F1. A $FF in the path list jumps to a new address; $80 in a velocity list sets $12B1 to read the next segment.
Slot 2's mover: as enemy_move_1, with this slot's variables ($11E2 alive, $12AA exploding, $1072 shot, $1222 icon touched, $1252/$125A path, $1262/$126A velocities).
Slot 3's mover: as enemy_move_1, with this slot's variables ($11E3 alive, $12AB exploding, $1073 shot, $1223 icon touched, $1253/$125B path, $1263/$126B velocities).
Slot 4's mover: as enemy_move_1, with this slot's variables ($11E4 alive, $12AC exploding, $1074 shot, $1224 icon touched, $1254/$125C path, $1264/$126C velocities).
Slot 5's mover: as enemy_move_1, with this slot's variables ($11E5 alive, $12AD exploding, $1075 shot, $1225 icon touched, $1255/$125D path, $1265/$126D velocities).
Slot 6's mover: as enemy_move_1, with this slot's variables ($11E6 alive, $12AE exploding, $1076 shot, $1226 icon touched, $1256/$125E path, $1266/$126E velocities).
Slot 7's mover: as enemy_move_1, with this slot's variables ($11E7 alive, $12AF exploding, $1077 shot, $1227 icon touched, $1257/$125F path, $1267/$126F velocities).

Before the movers: when the wave's timer $129E runs (and $129D is set) counts it down; at zero, or when slot 1 holds an enemy that cannot be destroyed ($1241 = $FF) and slot 7 has just been destroyed ($1077 set and its hit points $1247 at zero), every enemy is marked as shot ($1070 + x) with its hit points zeroed, so the whole wave explodes: shooting the boss in slot 7 destroys its escort. Then the movers ($82AB).
After the movers: clears the per-slot 'hit' and 'icon touched' flags ($1070, $1220) and $129D, then applies the velocities ($80E1).
Adds the points of an enemy (A) to the pending score: 100 ($64) adds one to the hundreds digit $11D4; otherwise tens go into $11D5 and units into $11D6.

Wave type 1 handler (through $9F20): counts $1290 down; while the group has enemies left ($128C) advances $129C (wrapping at 7) and $128F, and spawns another ($80C9) every call until $128F reaches $20 (the operand at $90AE, patched per stage by s_9E40); then clears the type.

Spawn handler for type 1 (through $9F30): unless $1290 is running, gives the new enemy a spawn delay of 1; sets $1290 from $A701 + $43F6.
Spawn handler for type 0 (through $9F30): nothing.
Forty-two zero bytes, unused.

Sets this frame's enemy-fire rules, at the top of the play frame. The aiming coarseness comes from the stage's entry at $FA00 plus the weapon levels of icons 4 and 6 ($0F03, $0F05), capped at 3, through $9FE1 into the shift counts at $92EF and $9310. The kind of fire goes into $0F4D: bit 7 (the eight-way bullets) when $0F7A is clear or the orbiter (icon 5) is not owned, bit 6 (the bombs) when the shield (icon 7) is owned or the wave is $6E, low bits the base. Unless slot 1 holds a special enemy ($1201), the fire budget $0F74 comes from the stage (capped at 15, one more while the wave timer runs) through $9F10 and $9F08; otherwise it is $24. Then sets the icon colours.

Starts the game-over screen: fades on ($112A, $112C), $43C6 = 1, shop, hit and purchase flags cleared, the hazard-row speed operands at $2415/$24D3 set to 3, sprites 1-8 Y to 3, the ship's weapons cleared, the stars moved, tune $0C queued ($117D), and the panel sprites set (irq_panel_sprites).
Points the banner at the message table at $FB70 (both the drawer's $3BB3 and the centring's $3DA0), lines 3, 0, 1, 2, and centres it.
Stores Y in $1084, $9FF0 and $9FF1.
Queues tune $0C and sets up the name-entry sprites.
Three NOPs and four zero bytes, unused.
After a stage is cleared: moves on to the next stage ($107D); after stage 32 ($20) goes to the end of the game ($9D00), otherwise sets the next stage up.
Eight NOPs after stage_advance, unused.

Each frame one enemy slot (cycling 1-7 through $12DA) may fire: it must be alive, past its entry ($12B9 clear), allowed to fire (bit 6 of its speed byte $12E9), not exploding, and to the right of the ship's area (X under $48 with the high bit, or above $18); its own counter $12E1 + slot must reach the stage's rate $12DB. Then works out its cell, toggles $0F7A and, by $0F4D: bit 7 or the 'no aimed fire' state fires bullets ($945E), bit 6 a bomb ($938B), otherwise an aimed row shot: the step from the enemy towards the ship ($8D, $8E) is reduced by repeated halving to a direction ($12DD, $12F4) and a free shot slot is used (six, or two bombs), as long as the total in flight ($0F73: 5 per shot, 10 per bomb, 1 per bullet) stays under the budget $0F74. Queues the firing sound ($9EE0).
25 NOPs inside enemy_fire_decide, jumped over by its branch.

enemy_fire_decide, continued: the slot may fire: works out its cell and screen address, picks the kind of fire and the direction towards the ship, and launches a shot, a bomb or a bullet within the budget.

Immediate of the second CPX #$03 in the aiming, patched with $92EF.

Fires a bomb (2x2 characters, two at most, $0F71): same budget test (10 each); sets its column from the enemy, its column step from $0F93/$0F9C by the direction, its row step from the stored $0F90, and its screen pointer ($F4/$F6).

Fires an eight-way bullet (seven at most, $0F72; costs 1 of the budget): a free slot of seven ($10D9-$10DF) gets the column and row steps $12DD/$12F4, its column (enemy + 2) and row, and its screen pointer ($1A + 2 x slot).
Aims a bullet: with bit 7 of the fire kind straight along the row (row step 0), otherwise diagonally towards the ship; then enemy_fire_bullet.
Counts $43F2 down and redraws the lives digit.

The music player, once a frame (from sfx_queue_service): a driver in the style of Rob Hubbard's. Sets the volume to 15. Bit 7 of the control byte $C32E: silence the voices (once, then wait); bit 6: (re)start the tune set up by set_tune, zeroing each voice's state. Otherwise, every tick (speed $C32B, counted by $C310, with a further divider $C32C) for each voice 2..0: when its note ends, reads the voice's track ($C4EE/$C4F1: pattern numbers, $FF to loop, $FE to stop; a number below $80 is a repeat count) and the current pattern (through $C542/$C5AF): duration and flags, an optional instrument (into $C2FE) or portamento, the note (looked up in the frequency table $C226), and loads the instrument's pulse width, control, attack/decay and sustain/release from its record at $C38E + 8 x instrument. Every frame applies the instrument's effects ($C393-$C395 and the second record at $C43E): vibrato, pulse-width sweep, portamento, drum and arpeggio-style waveform/pitch changes, the filter sweep, and releases the gate before the note ends; writes control, frequency and pulse to the SID.
